assertions.description: color() accepts display-p3-linear as a predefined color space keyword.
display-p3-linear components accept percentages (0% = 0.0, 100% = 1.0) and an alpha channel.
display-p3-linear is a <rectangular-color-space>, so color-mix() accepts it as an interpolation space.
Gradients accept 'in display-p3-linear' as their color interpolation method.
A display-p3-linear color round-trips through getComputedStyle serialized in its own color space with its components intact.
Components outside [0, 1] are valid in color(display-p3-linear ...) and are stored unclamped for later gamut mapping.
Converting the spec's example color(display-p3-linear 0.3081 0.014 0.0567) to display-p3 via relative color syntax yields the spec's stated twin, 0.591 0.123 0.264.
assertions.test: (()=>{const e=document.createElement('span');e.style.color='color(from color(display-p3-linear 0.3081 0.014 0.0567) display-p3 r g b)';if(!e.style.color)return false;document.body.appendChild(e);const v=getComputedStyle(e).color;e.remove();const n=(v.match(/-?\d*\.?\d+/g)||[]).map(Number).slice(-3);return n.length===3&&Math.abs(n[0]-0.591)<0.005&&Math.abs(n[1]-0.123)<0.005&&Math.abs(n[2]-0.264)<0.005;})()
